extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_short: asserting small and micro entity status
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for establishing, changing, correcting, and refunding small-entity and micro-entity patent fee status (who may assert, how an assertion may be made, investigative duties, error correction, and micro-entity eligibility rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion requirement for small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent to assert small entity status must be clearly indicated in order to comply with the assertion requirement; no specific words or wording are required to assert small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear written assertion is required (words not prescribed). If an exact small-entity basic filing or basic national fee is paid, that payment may be treated as a written assertion (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties who can sign the written assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: The written assertion can be signed by: (i) one of the parties identified in § 1.33(b) (e.g., a registered attorney or agent), (ii) at least one individual identified as an inventor (even without a § 1.63 executed oath/declaration), or (iii) an assignee of an undivided part interest (with limits on filing by partial assignees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial assignees may sign but cannot file the assertion without resort to a party identified under § 1.33(b). Pre-AIA rules provide similar but slightly different filing/signing distinctions (see MPEP § 509.03 III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a signed written assertion (pre-AIA distinctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, one of several inventors may both sign and file a written assertion, but a partial assignee may sign yet the assertion must be filed by an appropriate party under pre-AIA § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with three pro se inventors, one inventor filing the application can submit and establish small entity status for that application; where rights are divided among different types of entities, a single party's assertion suffices if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by payment of exact small-entity basic filing or basic national fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the exact amount of one of the small entity basic filing fees (§§ 1.16(a)-(e)) or the small entity basic national fee (§ 1.492(a)) will be treated as a written assertion of entitlement to small entity status, even if the type of fee selected was inadvertently incorrect for that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office accords small entity status based on such payment that is not applicable, any balance due must be paid with applicable surcharges (§ 1.16(f) or (g)). Payment of other small-entity fees (extension, issue, reexamination, etc.) or an incorrect amount is not treated as an assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of wrong fee type or incorrect amount does not by itself establish small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of any small entity fee other than the exact small-entity basic filing, basic national, or individual designation fee (or paying an incorrect fee amount) will not be treated as a written assertion of entitlement to small entity status and will not be sufficient to establish status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exact small-entity basic filing/national/individual designation fee is paid but wrong type selected, applicant must still pay any balance due; general authorizations to charge fees do not suffice to pay small-entity amounts unless specifically directed to small-entity fee types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion required in each related, continuing, and reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Status as a small entity must be specifically established by an assertion in each related, continuing, and reissue application in which status is appropriate and desired; status in one application or patent does not affect others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refiling as a continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part (including CPA), or filing a reissue requires a new assertion of continued entitlement to small entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties who can establish small entity status by payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where small entity status is sought by payment of the basic filing fee, basic national fee, or individual designation fee, any party (including a third party) may submit payment and small entity status will be accorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment by any party (e.g., check) of the exact small-entity basic filing/national/individual designation fee operates as the assertion for that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to investigate entitlement to small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants need to do a complete and thorough investigation of all facts and circumstances before determining and asserting entitlement to small entity status; where entitlement is uncertain it should not be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation should include consulting co-inventors about assignments/licensing and, for business concerns, review of size standards in 13 CFR 121.801–121.805. Costs of investigation may outweigh benefits; the person asserting should be in a position to know the facts and must be able to unequivocally self-certify.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO will not give advisory opinions on entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office does not give advisory opinions as to whether a specific individual or organization qualifies as a small entity; establishing reduced fees is based on self-certification under 37 CFR 1.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the required assertion is the applicant's self-certification of entitlement; reliance on oral advice from USPTO employees is not appropriate to establish entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change/Removal of small entity status and required notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Once small entity status is established, it may be used until the earliest of the issue fee or any maintenance fee due; notification of any change resulting in loss of entitlement must be filed prior to or at the time of paying that earliest fee and must be a specific written assertion of loss of entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When paying an issue fee after status has changed, applicant should (A) check the appropriate box on Part B of PTOL-85 to indicate loss of small entity status and (B) pay the non-small-entity fee amount. Failure to file the written notification is noncompliant under § 1.27(g)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraudulent establishment of small entity status is treated as fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attempt to fraudulently establish small entity status or pay fees as a small entity will be considered a fraud practiced or attempted on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office normally will not question a claim to small entity status, but intentional misrepresentation can have serious consequences; applicants should not rely on oral advice from USPTO employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds when small entity status later established (37 CFR 1.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: A refund based on later establishment of small entity status may be obtained under § 1.28(a) only if an assertion under § 1.27(c) and a request for refund are filed within three months of the date the full (non-small-entity) fee was paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-month period is not extendable under § 1.136. Date of payment (date full fee paid or date of receipt for authorizations) determines start of the three-month window; mailing methods (Certificate of Mailing, Priority Mail Express) have specific rules for receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excusing errors in small entity status (37 CFR 1.28(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If small entity status was established and fees paid in good faith but later discovered to be erroneous, the error will be excused upon compliance with separate submission and itemization requirements and payment of the deficiency owed as set out in 37 CFR 1.28(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: (1) separate submission limited to one application or patent per paper, (2) payment of per-fee deficiency amounts, and (3) itemization of each fee involved. Failure to comply permits Office to charge processing fee or require one-month compliance to avoid return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of deficiency owed for erroneous small-entity payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The deficiency for each previous fee erroneously paid as a small entity is the difference between the current non-small-entity fee amount on the date the deficiency is paid in full and the amount of the previous erroneous small-entity payment; if a fee decreased, the deficiency owed equals the amount previously paid in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total deficiency is the sum of individual deficiencies. The itemization must include: (A) fee type, (B) small-entity fee actually paid and date, (C) deficiency owed for each fee, and (D) total deficiency owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of deficiency operates as notification of loss of status
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deficiency payment submitted under 37 CFR 1.28(c) will be treated under § 1.27(g)(2) as a notification of loss of entitlement to small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fees improperly paid as small entity where status is no longer appropriate are treated under § 1.28(c) and will not cause patent expiration under § 1.378; by contrast, paying a small-entity maintenance fee without established status may cause expiration unless full fee or written assertion is timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity statutory definition (35 U.S.C. 123 criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: For micro entity status an applicant must certify that they: (1) qualify as a small entity; (2) have not been named as inventor on more than four previous patent applications (with specified exclusions); (3) did not have gross income in the preceding calendar year exceeding three times the median household income; and (4) have not assigned/granted/licensed (and are not obligated to do so) rights to an entity whose gross income in the preceding year exceeded three times the median household income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition incorporates income and filing-count limits and includes exclusions for certain prior-filed applications (foreign, provisional, PCT where national fee not paid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications resulting from prior employment exception for micro-entity counting
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is not considered to be named on a previously filed application for purposes of the four-application limit if the applicant has assigned, or is under an obligation by contract or law to assign, all ownership rights in the application as the result of the applicant’s previous employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits counting of prior applications that were assigned away due to employment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign currency exchange rate for micro-entity income thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant’s or entity’s gross income in the preceding calendar year is not in U.S. dollars, the average currency exchange rate reported by the IRS during that calendar year shall be used to determine whether gross income exceeds the micro-entity thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IRS average exchange rate for the relevant calendar year to convert to U.S. dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions of higher education inclusion as micro entities
rubrics_metrics.description: A micro entity includes an applicant who certifies either that (1) the applicant’s employer (from which the applicant obtains the majority of income) is an institution of higher education, or (2) the applicant has assigned/granted/conveyed or is under obligation to assign/grant/convey a license or other ownership interest in the particular application to such an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution of higher education is as defined in the Higher Education Act (20 U.S.C. 1001(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to impose additional micro-entity limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may, in the Director’s discretion, impose income limits, annual filing limits, or other limits on who may qualify as a micro entity if reasonably necessary to avoid undue impact on other applicants or otherwise appropriate, with notice to Congressional Judiciary Committees at least three months before such limits take effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an additional administrative safeguard beyond statutory text; proposals must be communicated to Committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for false micro-entity certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity found to have falsely made a micro-entity certification shall be subject to a fine, at least three times the amount that the entity failed to pay as a result of the false certification, as determined by the Director, in addition to any other available penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The penalty applies whether the false certification is discovered before or after issuance of a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement and timing for micro-entity certification filing
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 123 requires a written certification for micro-entity status filed prior to or at the time a fee is first paid in the micro-entity amount in an application or patent; a fee may be paid in the micro-entity amount only if submitted with, or subsequent to, the submission of a certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status in one application does not affect other applications; a new certification is required for continuations, divisionals, CIP (and reissue) and micro-entity certification may be filed in pending applications, reexamination (patent owner only), supplemental examination, and patents prior to or with maintenance fee payment. Attempts to fraudulently establish micro-entity status treated as fraud (37 CFR 1.29(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees covered by the micro-entity discount
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-entity discounts (80% as of recent statutory/regulatory updates) apply to filing fees (provisional and nonprovisional), search fees, examination fees, issue fees, appeal fees, and patent maintenance fees (including grace-period surcharges and certain surcharge petitions), across utility, design, plant, and reissue applications; also include application-related fees like excess claims, application size fees, non-DOCX filing surcharge, and certain surcharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included examination fees extend to prioritized examination (1.102(e)), ex parte reexamination requests filed by a patent owner, and supplemental examination. Appeal fees include notice of appeal, forwarding appeal to PTAB, and requesting an oral hearing. Some international/PCT/Hague timing rules specify effective dates for increased discounts.
